title: Excel specifications and limits
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 1,048,576 rows by 16,384 columns; 15-digit precision; formula length 8,192 characters; 64 nesting levels; 255 arguments; applies to Excel for Microsoft 365, 2024, 2021, 2019 and 2016.

title: XLOOKUP function
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Syntax; exact match by default; if_not_found argument; binary search needs sorted data; not available in Excel 2016 and Excel 2019.

title: LET function
supports: Opened with WebFetch. LET names calculation results inside a formula; up to 126 name and value pairs; a repeated expression is calculated once; Microsoft 365, Excel 2024 and Excel 2021.

title: LAMBDA function
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Custom functions with no VBA; named LAMBDAs in Name Manager; up to 253 parameters; applies to Microsoft 365 and Excel 2024, not Excel 2021.

title: Dynamic array formulas and spilled array behavior
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Results spill into neighbouring cells; #SPILL! when the range is blocked; spilled array formulas are not supported in Excel tables.

title: Floating-point arithmetic may give inaccurate result in Excel
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 15 Apr 2026). Excel follows IEEE 754 with 15 digits of precision; 0.1 cannot be stored exactly; use ROUND; Set precision as displayed permanently loses data.

title: Using structured references with Excel tables
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Structured references use table and column names and adjust automatically when rows or columns are added, removed or renamed.

title: Apply data validation to cells
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Validation types (whole number, decimal, list, date, time, text length, custom); Stop alerts force a fix; settings cannot be changed when the sheet is protected or the workbook shared.

title: Protect a worksheet
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Worksheet level protection isn't intended as a security feature; cells are locked by default; Microsoft cannot retrieve a forgotten password.

title: Set automatic data conversions
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Four conversions can be turned off (leading zeros, 15-digit truncation, E notation, letters and numbers to dates); File > Options > Data; Excel for Microsoft 365 and Excel 2024.

title: Excel performance: Tips for optimizing performance obstructions
supports: Opened with WebFetch (dated 11 Nov 2025). Minimise the used range; avoid volatile OFFSET and INDIRECT; prefer SUMIFS over SUMPRODUCT arrays; in VBA turn off screen updating, manual calculation and events, then restore; read and write ranges as arrays.

title: Macros from the internet are blocked by default in Office
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 31 Jul 2026). Office on Windows blocks macros in files with the Mark of the Web; Current Channel 2206 from 27 Jul 2022; not Mac, mobile or web; Trusted Locations used sparingly; recommended baseline allows only digitally signed macros from trusted publishers.

title: Migrate scripts to the V8 runtime
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The Rhino runtime was deprecated on 31 January 2026; existing Rhino scripts must be migrated to V8; list of Rhino-only features that need changes.

title: Option Explicit statement
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Option Explicit forces explicit declaration of all variables; an undeclared name causes a compile-time error; helps avoid mistyped variable names.

title: Differences between Office Scripts and VBA macros
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 16 Nov 2023). Office Scripts run on web, Windows, Mac and Power Automate and only access the workbook; VBA is desktop only with no Power Automate connector; Office Scripts have no workbook events; licence wording.

title: Get started with Copilot in Excel
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Allow editing (default), Plan and Chat only modes; platform support for Windows, Mac, web, iPad, iPhone and Android.

title: What's New in Excel (February 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (24 Feb 2026). Agent Mode in Copilot in Excel became available to EU customers on Current Channel and Monthly Enterprise Channel; UK not mentioned.

title: COPILOT function
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The COPILOT function is no longer available from 14 September 2026; it was preview only; cached results stay but cells return #NAME? on recalculation.

title: Quotas for Google Services
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 6 minutes per execution; trigger runtime 90 min a day (consumer) and 6 hours (Workspace); email recipients 100 and 1,500 a day; quotas may change without notice.

title: Best practices (Apps Script)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Minimise service calls; batch reads and writes; example of about 70 seconds cell by cell versus about 1 second batched; use the Cache service.

title: Installable triggers
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Installable triggers always run under the account of the person who created them; time-driven triggers from every minute to monthly; start times can vary within the chosen hour.

title: Authorization scopes (Apps Script)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Scopes are detected automatically and may be broader than needed; set oauthScopes in appsscript.json; always use the least permissive scope set possible.

title: Files you can store in Google Drive
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Google Sheets files hold up to 20 million cells or 100 MB.

title: Protect, hide, and edit sheets
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Protected ranges can show a warning or restrict editors; protection should not be used as a security measure because people with access can still copy and export data.

title: Use the AI function in Google Sheets
supports: Opened with WebFetch. AI function sees only the given range; first 350 selected cells per selection; manual refresh; may suggest inaccurate information.

title: Audits of operational spreadsheets
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Known-methodology audits found errors in 84% of 163 spreadsheets (83% in the table); core studies found serious errors in 91% of 55; single inspectors caught 34% to 69% of errors.

title: Spreadsheet development experiments
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Individuals working alone had a cell error rate of 3.2% (1.1% to 5.6% across studies); groups of three or more reduced errors; people have poor intuition about their own error rates.

title: The FAST Standard
supports: Opened with WebFetch. FAST means Flexible, Appropriate, Structured, Transparent; current version 02c (July 2019), released under a Creative Commons licence.

title: Does High Public Debt Consistently Stifle Economic Growth? A Critique of Reinhart and Rogoff (Working Paper 322, April 2013)
publisher: Political Economy Research Institute, University of Massachusetts Amherst
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A spreadsheet error left out Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada and Denmark; corrected average growth above 90% debt was 2.2%, not -0.1%.

title: Gene name errors are widespread in the scientific literature (Genome Biology 17, 177, 2016)
publisher: Ziemann, Eren and El-Osta, Genome Biology (Springer Nature)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Excel default settings convert gene symbols such as SEPT2 and MARCH1 to dates; errors in 704 of the articles with Excel gene lists, about 19.6%.
